metadata.title: Antibiotic Checkerboard Synergy Assay (FIC Index) in a 96-Well Plate
metadata.purpose: Determine whether two antimicrobial agents (drug A x drug B) act synergistically, indifferently, or antagonistically against a bacterial isolate by testing a two-dimensional grid of 2-fold serial-dilution combinations across a 96-well plate and computing the Fractional Inhibitory Concentration (FIC) index.
metadata.scope: Broth-microdilution checkerboard for two-drug combinations against a single aerobic bacterial isolate, following the simplified multichannel method of Bellio et al. (2021) with CLSI/EUCAST-referenced media and inoculum, and FIC-index interpretation per Odds (2003). Out of scope: three-drug combinations, time-kill kinetics, anaerobes/fastidious organisms requiring special atmospheres, and fully automated (inkjet) dispensing.
metadata.estimatedTime: ~3 days (Day 1: media + stocks + overnight culture; Day 2: plate setup + inoculation + 18 h incubation; Day 3: OD reading + analysis)
beforeYouBegin: Choose the two drugs and, from prior single-drug MICs, set each drug's highest tested concentration to at least 2x-4x its standalone MIC so the FIC index can be computed.

Decide the plate orientation: drug A is serially diluted DOWN the rows (A high -> G low), drug B is serially diluted ACROSS the columns (column 12 high -> column 2 low); row H is drug-B-alone and column 1 is drug-A-alone.
Prepare a mirror (no-bacteria) plate with identical reagents to serve as the sterility / OD-background control.
Confirm the biosafety level required for your isolate with your institution before beginning.
metadata.license: Method transcribed from an open-access (CC-BY) MethodsX article; verify reuse terms at record level.

materials.specification: Diluted 1:2 by the aqueous drug/inoculum additions to reach 1x final in the well

materials.rawText: Two antimicrobics or compounds from stock solutions or powder.

materials.specification: From stock solution or powder; dissolved in the CLSI/EUCAST-recommended solvent/diluent for that agent. Specific agent and concentration range depend on the user's combination.
materials.rawText: Two antimicrobics or compounds from stock solutions or powder.

materials.specification: As specified in CLSI 'Solvents and Diluents for Preparing Stock Solutions of Antimicrobial Agents' or EUCAST guidance; agent-dependent.
materials.rawText: Diluents for the antimicrobial agent stock solutions.

materials.name: Bacterial isolate (isolated colonies)

samples.name: Bacterial isolate (input)

samples.name: Overnight MHB culture
samples.description: Colony grown 18 +/- 2 h at 35 +/- 2 C, 200 rpm; reaches ~1 x 10^9 CFU/mL.

samples.name: Standardized working inoculum

tables.title: Checkerboard axis layout (2D drug A x drug B combination grid)
rows: Down: A -> G (2-fold), discard 100 uL from G
tables.note: Every interior well (rows A-G x columns 2-12) is a DISTINCT A+B combination. Well H1 = growth control (no drug). Column 1 rows A-G = drug A dilution series alone. Row H columns 2-12 = drug B dilution series alone. Well A12 receives drug A as 2x-strength stock (2xS) so its concentration stays constant during the row dilution. There is no native schema construct for a 2D combinatorial well matrix; this table encodes it.

tables.title: Illustrative 2-fold concentration series (SET TO YOUR OWN MICs before use)
rows: Step 7 (lowest, drug A only to row G)
tables.note: Placeholder ratios only - the source is a method paper that does not fix specific drugs/concentrations. Choose the highest tested concentration >= 2x-4x each drug's standalone MIC. Units (e.g. ug/mL) depend on the agents. needsReview.

tables.title: FIC index (Sum-FIC) interpretation
tables.note: Per Odds (2003), who recommends these three categories. Many labs subdivide the middle band as >0.5-1.0 additive and >1.0-4.0 indifferent; report whichever scheme you adopt. FIC index = (MIC of A in combination / MIC of A alone) + (MIC of B in combination / MIC of B alone).

tables.title: Control wells / lanes
rows: Drug A alone MIC (denominator for FIC_A)
Drug B alone MIC (denominator for FIC_B)

steps.action: Weigh and dissolve MHB, CAMHB and 2x CAMHB powders in deionised water per package insert using a magnetic stirrer, then sterilise by autoclaving.

parameters.rawText: autoclaving at 121 C for 15 min
for 15 min

steps.expectedResult: Sterile MHB, CAMHB and 2x CAMHB ready.

sourceReferences.excerpt: dissolve the powder ... sterilise by autoclaving at 121 C for 15 min.

steps.action: Prepare 100 mL sterile 0.9% saline: dissolve 0.9 g NaCl in 100 mL deionised water and autoclave.

parameters.rawText: 0.9 g of NaCl
into 100 mL of deionised water

steps.action: Prepare stock solutions of drug A and drug B by dissolving each powder in its CLSI/EUCAST-recommended solvent/diluent (or the solvent that maximises stability if not listed).
steps.criticalNotes: Specific solvent and stock concentration are agent-dependent and must be confirmed against CLSI/EUCAST tables or the datasheet.

sourceReferences.excerpt: dissolve each one into its appropriate solvent as requested by CLSI ... or as recommended by the EUCAST guidelines.

steps.action: Inoculate one isolated colony into 10 mL MHB and grow overnight in an orbital shaker-incubator under aerobic conditions.

parameters.rawText: into a 10 mL of MHB
orbital shaker incubator at 200 rpm
for 18 h +/- 2
the culture will reach the concentration of ~ 10^9 CFU/mL

steps.action: Dispense 100 uL of 2x CAMHB into every well of the 96-well assay plate using a multichannel pipette, proceeding column by column.

parameters.rawText: Place 100 uL of the 2 x CAMHB medium ... dispense into each well

sourceReferences.excerpt: Place 100 uL of the 2 x CAMHB medium in a V-shaped reservoir ... dispense into each well of the microplate.

steps.action: Prepare drug A working stocks in 2x CAMHB: 1.5 mL of stock S at 4x the highest tested concentration, and 500 uL of 2xS at 8x the highest tested concentration.

parameters.rawText: Prepare 1.5 mL of stock solution (S)
4-fold more concentrated than the highest concentration of the drug A
Prepare 500 uL of 2 x stock solution (2 x S)
8-fold more concentrated than the highest concentration of the drug A

steps.expectedResult: Drug A S and 2xS stocks ready.
steps.criticalNotes: The 2xS aliquot is added to well A12 so drug A concentration stays constant there during the row serial dilution.

steps.action: Dispense 100 uL of drug A stock S into row A, columns 1-11; dispense 100 uL of drug A 2xS into well A12.

parameters.rawText: Dispense 100 uL of S into row A from columns 1-11.
Dispense 100 uL of 2 x S into well A12.

steps.expectedResult: Row A loaded with drug A (highest concentration).

steps.action: Serially dilute drug A DOWN the plate from row A to row G (transfer 100 uL, mix), discarding the final 100 uL taken from row G. Change tips between the two halves if using an 8-channel pipette.

parameters.rawText: multichannel pipette set to 100 uL
two-fold serial dilution A -> G

steps.expectedResult: 2-fold decreasing drug A gradient across rows A (high) to G (low); row H has no drug A.
steps.criticalNotes: Discard the remaining volume from row G so row H stays drug-A-free.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Dilute the drug A from row A to G ... and discard the remaining volume from row G.

steps.action: Prepare 1.0 mL of drug B stock S in 2x CAMHB at 4x the highest tested concentration, then dispense 100 uL into every well of column 12.

parameters.rawText: Prepare 1.0 mL of stock solution (S)
4-fold more concentrated than the highest concentration of drug B
Dispense 100 uL of S into each column 12 wells.

steps.expectedResult: Column 12 loaded with drug B (highest concentration).

steps.action: Serially dilute drug B ACROSS the plate from column 12 to column 2 (transfer 100 uL, mix), discarding the final 100 uL taken from column 2.

parameters.rawText: multichannel pipette set to 100 uL
two-fold serial dilution column 12 -> 2

steps.expectedResult: 2-fold decreasing drug B gradient from column 12 (high) to column 2 (low); column 1 has no drug B. Interior wells now hold every A x B combination.
steps.criticalNotes: Discard the remaining volume from column 2 so column 1 stays drug-B-free.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Dilute the drug B Column 12-2 ... and discard the remaining volume taken from column 2.

steps.action: Prepare 10-40 mL of bacterial inoculum at ~1 x 10^6 CFU/mL in 0.9% NaCl from the overnight culture (vortex >= 20 s first), then dispense 100 uL into every well of the assay plate. Set up a mirror plate with the same reagents but no bacteria.

parameters.rawText: Prepare from 10 to 40 mL of bacterial inoculum
Place 100 uL of inoculum ... dispense into each well
The final inoculum concentration in the microplate will be 5 x 10^5 CFU/mL

steps.expectedResult: Every well at 200 uL total, 1x CAMHB, final inoculum 5 x 10^5 CFU/mL; mirror plate prepared.
steps.criticalNotes: Final volume per well is 200 uL; the 1:2 addition brings 2x CAMHB and drug stocks to 1x working strength.

steps.action: Cover and incubate the assay plate (and mirror plate) statically at 35 +/- 2 C for 18 +/- 2 h. Seal with film and/or add a water tray to limit evaporation if needed.

parameters.rawText: static incubator at 35 +/- 2 C
for 18 +/- 2 h

steps.expectedResult: Growth in the no-drug control (H1); inhibition in effective combinations.

steps.action: Mix the contents of each well with a multichannel pipette, then read optical density at 600 nm (or 595/605 nm) on a microplate reader; read the mirror plate for background.

parameters.rawText: Read the optical density (OD) at 600 nm or around 600 nm (e.g. 595 or 605).

steps.expectedResult: OD600 value recorded for all 96 wells (assay and mirror).

steps.action: Compute percent growth per well (background-subtracted, relative to the H1 growth control) and read the MIC of each drug alone and of each combination as the lowest concentration reducing growth by more than 80%.

parameters.rawText: MIC is defined as the lowest drug concentration, which reduces bacterial growth by more than 80%.
% growth = (OD_well - OD_background) / (OD_growth_control - OD_background) x 100 (exact formula not reproduced in source text)

steps.expectedResult: MIC_A alone, MIC_B alone, and the MIC of each drug within its most effective combination.
steps.criticalNotes: The percent-growth equation was not captured verbatim from the source (rendered as omitted); the form given here is the standard background-subtracted normalisation - verify against the source before reporting.

steps.action: Compute the FIC index for the combination and classify the interaction as synergy, no interaction, or antagonism.

parameters.rawText: FIC index = (MIC of A in combination / MIC of A alone) + (MIC of B in combination / MIC of B alone)

steps.expectedResult: A numeric FIC index and its interpretation (e.g. FIC <= 0.5 => synergy).
steps.criticalNotes: Use the lowest Sum-FIC among wells on the growth/no-growth boundary (the 'turbidity edge'). Loewe-additivity and Bliss-independence surface models can also be applied for a fuller picture.

sourceReferences.excerpt: FIC index <= 0.5 synergy; > 0.5 to 4.0 no interaction; > 4.0 antagonism.

controls.name: Positive growth control (well H1)
controls.description: Medium + inoculum, no drug; defines 100% growth and confirms viability.

controls.name: Drug A alone (column 1, rows A-G)
controls.description: Drug A serial dilution without drug B; yields MIC_A alone (FIC_A denominator).

controls.name: Drug B alone (row H, columns 2-12)
controls.description: Drug B serial dilution without drug A; yields MIC_B alone (FIC_B denominator).

controls.name: Mirror sterility / background plate
controls.description: All reagents, no bacteria; checks sterility and provides OD background for subtraction, including drug precipitation artifacts.

controls.name: QC reference strain (recommended)
controls.description: Run a CLSI/EUCAST QC strain with known MIC to validate the run.

expectedOutputs: OD600 map of the 96-well combination grid.
MIC of drug A alone, drug B alone, and within combination.
A computed FIC index and a synergy/no-interaction/antagonism call.
Optional Loewe/Bliss interaction analysis across the surface.

troubleshooting.problem: No growth in the H1 control
troubleshooting.cause: Inoculum too dilute, non-viable, or wrong incubation
troubleshooting.solution: Re-verify inoculum density (0.5 McFarland -> 1:100/1:200 dilution), re-check 35 +/- 2 C incubation and colony viability
Discard, re-autoclave media, remake drug stocks with sterile technique
Seal plate with film and/or add a water tray to the incubator

troubleshooting.problem: FIC index differs between replicate runs
troubleshooting.cause: MIC is discontinuous over 2-fold steps; reading at a single boundary well is noisy
troubleshooting.solution: Run in duplicate/triplicate and report the range or median FIC
Subtract the mirror-plate background well-by-well; reduce the highest tested concentration

safety: Handle live bacterial cultures per the biosafety level assigned to your isolate; decontaminate plates and inoculum waste before disposal.
Some antimicrobial solvents (e.g. DMSO, DMF) and concentrated drug stocks are irritants/toxic - handle with gloves and follow SDS guidance.
Autoclave hot media and glassware with heat-resistant gloves.
limitations: The source is a simplified two-drug checkerboard method paper that does not fix specific antibiotics or concentration values; the concentration series here is illustrative and must be set to the user's drugs and MICs. MIC over 2-fold dilutions is coarse, so FIC-index category boundaries are inherently uncertain; the percent-growth equation and some inoculum exponents were not cleanly captured from the source text and are flagged needsReview. Not validated for anaerobes, three-drug combinations, or time-kill dynamics.

sources.title: New and simplified method for drug combination studies by checkerboard assay (Bellio et al., MethodsX 2021)
Synergy, antagonism, and what the chequerboard puts between them (Odds, J. Antimicrob. Chemother. 2003) - FIC index interpretation
